title: POC scoping — private networking & data residency (Veridian Health)
summary: Redwood AE/SE introduced POC scope focused on private networking and data residency for Veridian Health.
Primary goals: validate VPC peering/PrivateLink connectivity, measure inference latency and egress constraints in region, and agree success criteria and timeline for 4-week POC.
Key constraints: PHI-sensitive data, must keep traffic within US-EAST-1 and US-WEST-2; strict egress policy, auditing/KMS requirements discussed.
Next steps: Redwood to share network diagram and PrivateLink checklist, customer to provide approximate qps and payload sizes, schedule pilot benchmark run week 3.
topics: workload sizing: qps, max tokens, concurrency
next_steps: Samira to send PrivateLink checklist + sample VPC peering diagram (by 2027-10-07)
Veridian: provide 2-week historic qps and payload distribution (by 2027-10-05)
Diego to propose benchmark plan (latency, p99, throughput) and required agent/container specs (by 2027-10-08)
action_items: Owner: Samira Patel; Item: Share Redwood private networking quickstart & PrivateLink checklist; Due: 2027-10-07
Owner: Tom Becker; Item: Export sample traffic profile (qps, avg/max request size, typical prompt lengths); Due: 2027-10-05
Owner: Diego Morales; Item: Draft benchmark plan with target SLA/p99, token accounting, and tooling (wrk/gRPC test harness); Due: 2027-10-08
Owner: Priya Shah; Item: Provide required compliance docs list (SOC2 scope, KMS/HSM requirements, data retention policy); Due: 2027-10-06
transcript: [00:00] Samira Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — Samira from Redwood here, joined by Diego on the SE side and Lena in CSM.
[00:08] Asha Nair: Hi all, this is Asha from Veridian. We have Tom and Priya as well, thanks for setting this up.
[00:15] Diego Morales: Quick agenda — confirm POC success criteria, discuss PrivateLink vs VPC peering, regions/data residency, sizing and benchmarks, and timeline.
[00:28] Tom Becker: Perfect. Our top requirement is that PHI data never leaves our AWS footprint — ideally traffic stays in us-east-1 or us-west-2 depending on the region for the tenant.
[00:40] Priya Shah: Also we have strict egress controls, any outbound connections must be controllable and logged. KMS for key management is required for model logs as well.
[00:52] Samira Patel: Totally understood. For the POC we can run either VPC peering or PrivateLink — both keep traffic inside AWS but differ in routing and maintenance. We'll outline the tradeoffs.

[01:08] Diego Morales: To add, PrivateLink avoids route table changes and central NAT, it terminates at an ENI in your VPC. VPC peering is simpler but can introduce route propagation issues across multiple accounts.
[01:25] Tom Becker: Do you support cross-account VPC peering? We have prod and analytics accounts separated.
[01:30] Samira Patel: Yes, we support cross-account peering. For multi-account setups we often recommend PrivateLink to reduce blast radius, but we'll diagram both options.
[01:45] Marcus Lee: On workload sizing: peak qps is about 180 requests/sec for our triage pipeline, avg token request is around 600 tokens, occasional spikes to 3k tokens for batch summaries.
[01:58] Diego Morales: That's helpful. For 180 qps at ~600 tokens, we'll want to run throughput benchmarks to estimate GPU footprints and batching settings. Any latency SLOs?
[02:10] Asha Nair: P99 under 400ms is ideal for triage, but for heavy batch jobs we tolerate higher latency. The interactive path needs tight latency.
[02:23] Priya Shah: Also audit logs are mandatory; we need request and response metadata stored in our audit system. Can Redwood push logs to our Kinesis/Splunk over a private endpoint?
[02:35] Samira Patel: We can stream telemetry to your endpoint over PrivateLink; Diego will confirm specific log formats and retention options.
[02:50] Tom Becker: Egress constraints — our security team blocks outbound 0.0.0.0/0 from prod subnets. How does Redwood handle callbacks and system updates that need outbound access?

[03:03] Diego Morales: Our agents typically initiate connections to Redwood control plane for management, but data plane traffic for inference stays on the private connection. For updates we can schedule maintenance windows or use a proxy in a guarded subnet.
[03:18] Priya Shah: We need to ensure no decryption of PHI outside our KMS. How do you manage key material? Can we use our customer-managed CMK/HSM?

[03:28] Samira Patel: Yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations are supported. For Private deployments we can configure keys to be customer-owned; we'll include the KMS integration steps in the docs.

[03:43] Asha Nair: Good. On success criteria — we propose: 1) verification of private connectivity in both accounts, 2) p99 latency < 400ms for triage workload at 180 qps during benchmark, 3) PHI never leaves approved regions, 4) audit logs flowing to our endpoint.
[04:00] Samira Patel: That sounds reasonable. We'll map each criterion to testable checks in the benchmark plan.

[04:12] Diego Morales: For benchmarks, we'll run a staged test: baseline small concurrency, then ramp to peak and sustained load. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization. We'll also test large token requests to validate KV cache and memory behavior.
[04:30] Marcus Lee: Do you have a suggested harness? We currently use a mix of k6 and internal gRPC clients.

[04:36] Diego Morales: We'll provide a sample wrk/grpc harness and a Docker image that mimics your payload distribution; we'll also instrument to push traces to your X-Ray or Jaeger if needed over private link.
[04:50] Tom Becker: About regions — can we pin the model to us-east-1 for triage and us-west-2 for West coast tenants? We need data residency per tenant.

[04:59] Samira Patel: Yes, Redwood supports region pinning and routing by tenant. For POC we can stand up endpoints in both regions; we'll show routing policy and fallback behavior if a region is constrained.
[05:12] Priya Shah: What's the expected timeline for the POC? We want a short pilot — four weeks ideally.

[05:18] Samira Patel: A four-week POC is doable. Week 1: network setup and connectivity validation; Week 2: baseline functional tests; Week 3: scale benchmarks; Week 4: cutover run and review + final report.
[05:30] Asha Nair: Is there a cost estimate for running the benchmark GPUs? We'll need budget approval.
[05:36] Samira Patel: We'll provide an estimate based on the sizing you gave; for the POC we can offer trial credits and a detailed cost model including expected tokens and GPU hours.
[05:48] Tom Becker: For PrivateLink we need to open specific ports — can you send the security group/port requirements?
[05:54] Diego Morales: Absolutely — we'll include a minimal inbound SG list, and recommended NACLs. Typically we use TLS on 443 with mTLS option if you require mutual auth.
[06:04] Priya Shah: mTLS would be preferred for additional assurance. Also we'd like to onboard a small synthetic dataset with PHI redaction to validate output handling.
[06:16] Samira Patel: We can support redaction testing. One caution: we recommend masking/scrubbing before sending to reduce risk — but we'll accept masked PHI for the POC.
[06:27] Marcus Lee: On telemetry, do we get token-level billing and latency traces per request? We need to correlate costs to endpoints/pipelines.
[06:34] Lena Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns per route/model and you can export detailed usage to your billing system via PrivateLink.
[06:46] Tom Becker: For the benchmark, what metrics should we collect on our side?
[06:50] Diego Morales: Collect request timestamps, request/response sizes, token counts, and p50/p95/p99 latency. Also capture retry rates and GPU metrics. We'll give an instrumentation checklist.
[07:04] Asha Nair: Who needs to be involved from Redwood during the pilot?
[07:08] Samira Patel: Diego will lead technical setup and run the benchmark with you; Lena will coordinate logistics and reporting; I'll handle commercial and success criteria sign-off.
[07:18] Priya Shah: Is there any PII/PHI logging on the Redwood side during the test? We need explicit guarantees around data retention and deletion after the pilot.

[07:26] Samira Patel: We'll include retention settings in the POC contract. By default we do not retain request/response payloads for private deployments unless you opt-in; logs can be streamed to your endpoint for storage under your controls.
[07:40] Tom Becker: Network detail: for PrivateLink we'll create NLB endpoints — do you require static IPs, or are DNS names sufficient for your side?

[07:47] Diego Morales: DNS names are fine; if you need static egress IPs we can discuss NAT or proxy patterns. For strict egress controls we often recommend using a proxy subnet that routes to our ENI.
[07:59] Marcus Lee: We also have a downstream service that must not see raw responses — can we use response streaming to an internal processor before persistence?
[08:06] Samira Patel: Yes, you can chain responses to an internal processor. We'll validate that the data path remains inside your VPC and provide guidance on chaining.
[08:18] Asha Nair: On success criteria again — we want an acceptance test that runs a representative sample at 75% of peak and verifies p99 and logs. Is that typical?
[08:27] Diego Morales: That's a good approach — run at 75% sustained and then a spike test. We'll include test definitions in the benchmark plan.
[08:35] Tom Becker: Any recommended model quantization or inference optimizations to help hit latency at token sizes ~600?
[08:41] Diego Morales: We can recommend quantized model variants and batching policies; sometimes smaller context windows and prefix caching help. We'll propose config knobs to trade latency vs cost.
[08:54] Priya Shah: For audit we need immutable logs with tamper evidence — can you sign logs or push to our S3 with object lock?
[09:02] Samira Patel: We can support pushing logs to your S3 and you can enable S3 object lock/Write Once Read Many (WORM) for immutability. We'll document the flow.
[09:15] Marcus Lee: When do we run the first connectivity test?
[09:18] Samira Patel: If your infra team is ready, we can do a lightweight connectivity smoke test within the next week — Tom, can you confirm availability?
[09:25] Tom Becker: We can do it next Tuesday. I'll block time and share the contact for the infra engineer.
[09:30] Samira Patel: Great. We'll send the checklist tonight. Anything else on compliance?
[09:35] Priya Shah: Please include SOC2 scope and evidence we can present to internal auditors — especially around key handling and access controls.
[09:44] Samira Patel: We'll attach SOC2 and our security whitepaper. For private deployments we can expand the scope as needed.
[09:52] Asha Nair: On the timeline — confirm weeks again so we align procurement and budget approvals.

[09:58] Samira Patel: Week 0 — prep and network changes; Week 1 — connectivity and smoke tests; Week 2 — functional and small-scale tests; Week 3 — benchmark ramp and sustained run; Week 4 — final review and acceptance.
[10:12] Tom Becker: What is acceptance gating? If p99 misses by 50ms, is that fail or pass with remediation?

[10:18] Samira Patel: We'll capture tolerances in the acceptance criteria. Typically a miss under 10% triggers remediation, larger misses require investigation and re-run. We'll capture thresholds in the POC doc.
[10:31] Diego Morales: For measurement we'll produce dashboards in Redwood Console and push a CSV of raw events to your S3 for independent verification.
[10:40] Marcus Lee: Logging volume — how much storage do you anticipate for a 1-week benchmark at our traffic?
[10:46] Diego Morales: Rough back-of-envelope: ~180 qps * 600 tokens * 7 days — but logs are metadata only unless you opt to persist full responses. We'll provide a sizing calc in the doc.
[10:58] Asha Nair: Ok. Anything else from team?
[11:02] Priya Shah: Please include the minimal IAM policy needed for the ENI/NLB setup so our security team can pre-approve.
[11:10] Samira Patel: We'll include a minimal IAM template and SG/NLB settings in the checklist.
[11:18] Tom Becker: I'd like to see an example traffic replay tool to mimic our spike patterns — can you provide that?
[11:23] Diego Morales: Yes, we'll include a replay tool and a Docker image configured to your profile once you share the trace sample.
[11:33] Asha Nair: Great. Let's recap next steps and owners.

[11:38] Samira Patel: Recap: Samira sends checklist and diagrams; Tom provides traffic profile; Diego drafts benchmark; Priya provides compliance list. We'll aim for connectivity test next Tuesday and a POC kickoff mid-October.
[11:52] Tom Becker: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:55] Samira Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the checklist. Bye.
[12:00] (call ends)
